season_futures#bowl_eligibility_rule.evidence: Re-audit after the re-patch. In the catalog, cfb.bowl_selection_state mechanism, rationale, measurement and raw_data[1] now use the 90 percent rolling two-year grants-in-aid average (56.7 per year, which is 0.9 x 63), countable_wins = FBS wins + min(1, qualifying FCS wins), and deserving = countable wins >= overall losses. This matches NCAA Proposal 2022-22 (Sep 2022 D-I Council: 80 -> 90 percent). season_futures stage s7 and required_data[4].fields[4] agree, and no '80%' or 'obsolete' text remains in the catalog or the CFB review records. I read the NCAA S3 PDFs directly. The FBSOC May 2026 report shows 2026-30 removing the descending multiyear-APR ordering of 5-7 alternates. The Jun 23-24 2026 Cabinet report lists 2026-30 with 'No action taken by the cabinet', so the FBSOC adoption stands as final, and 2026-31 (reclassifying FCS-to-FBS programs bowl-eligible) as 'Adopted. (Final)'. Both are consistent with the input. The remaining residuals (FCS aid averages unpublished; 2026-27 handbook not seen) are disclosed in unresolved bowl_eligibility_rule.
